## Consumer Liability Limits for Unauthorized Credit Card Use

### Core Liability Cap
Under 12 CFR 1026.12(b), a cardholder's liability for unauthorized credit card use shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of money, property, labor, or services obtained by the unauthorized use before notification to the card issuer [C:12CFR1026_1026.12_chunk_0001].

### Definition of 'Unauthorized Use'
Unauthorized use means use of a credit card by a person other than the cardholder who does not have actual, implied, or apparent authority for such use, and from which the cardholder receives no benefit [C:12CFR1026_1026.12_chunk_0001].

### Conditions That Must Be Met Before Any Liability Attaches
A cardholder can be held liable only if ALL of the following conditions are satisfied [C:12CFR1026_1026.12_chunk_0001]:
1. The credit card is an accepted credit card;
2. The card issuer has provided adequate notice of the cardholder's maximum potential liability (stating liability shall not exceed $50 or any lesser amount) and of the means to notify the issuer of loss or theft, describing a means of notification; and

If 10 or more credit cards are issued by one card issuer for use by employees of an organization, the card issuer and organization may agree to liability terms without regard to this section. # Rules Governing Payment of Interest on Interest-Bearing Deposit Accounts

The primary governing regulation is **12 CFR Part 1030** (Regulation DD / Truth in Savings Act). Section **1030.7** governs payment of interest, addressing permissible balance calculation methods, minimum balance requirements, compounding/crediting, and when interest begins and ends to accrue. Related disclosure obligations appear in 1030.4(b).

## 1. Definition of Interest (12 CFR 1030.2(n))
Interest is any payment to a consumer or to an account for the use of funds, calculated by applying a periodic rate to the balance. It does not include a bonus or consideration worth $10 or less during a year, the waiver or reduction of a fee, or the absorption of expenses [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0749_chunk_0001]. A bonus (over $10) is separately defined [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0748_chunk_0001].

## 2. Balance Calculation Methods (12 CFR 1030.7(a)(1))
An institution must calculate interest on the full amount of principal each day using either the daily balance method or the average daily balance method. The ending-balance, low-balance, and investable-balance methods are prohibited. Staff commentary permits a rate greater than 1/365 (e.g., 1/360) if applied 365 days a year; permits 1/366 or 1/365 for 366 days in a leap year; does not require interest after time accounts mature; and requires interest on funds even in inactive/dormant accounts [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0764_chunk_0001].

## 3. Minimum Balance to Earn Interest (12 CFR 1030.7(a)(2))
If a minimum balance is required to earn interest, the institution must use the same method to determine the minimum balance as it uses to calculate interest; an additional method unequivocally beneficial to the consumer is allowed. An institution may choose not to pay interest for days when the balance drops below the minimum. It must pay interest on the full balance that meets the minimum. Any computation method may be used for minimum balances not involving interest payment (e.g., fee assessment) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001].

## 4. Compounding and Crediting (12 CFR 1030.7(b))
No particular compounding/crediting frequency is required; institutions may compound annually, semi-annually, quarterly, monthly, daily, continuously, or on any other basis. An institution may choose not to pay accrued interest if the consumer closes the account before accrued interest is credited, provided it discloses this practice in the initial account disclosures (Staff Commentary 1030.7(b)-3) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

## 5. Date Interest Begins and Ends (12 CFR 1030.7(c))
Interest must begin to accrue no later than the business day on which the institution receives provisional credit for the funds, in accordance with Section 606 of the Expedited Funds Availability Act and Regulation CC Section 229.14. Interest accrues until the day funds are withdrawn [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0765_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0766_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001].

## 6. Related Disclosures (12 CFR 1030.4(b))
Institutions must disclose both the annual percentage yield and the interest rate using those terms; the frequency of compounding and crediting; and, where consumers will forfeit interest by closing an account before accrued interest is credited, a statement that interest will not be paid. They must also disclose minimum balance requirements, how the balance is determined, the balance computation method under 1030.7, and when interest begins to accrue on noncash deposits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0755_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0756_chunk_0001].

## 7. Regulation vs. Examination Guidance
The rules above reflect the regulatory requirements of 12 CFR Part 1030 and its official Staff Commentary. The CFPB examination procedures and checklists [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0789_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0803_chunk_0001][C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0804_chunk_0001] are supervisory guidance used to verify compliance and do not create obligations beyond the regulation and commentary.
